content.text: {"jurisdiction":"united_states","issuing_body":"White House Office of Science and Technology Policy","document_type":"strategy_paper","binding_strength":"voluntary_commitment","publication_date":"2022-10","effective_date":null,"covered_application_domains":["general_purpose_models","critical_infrastructure","biometrics","public_sector_use","employment","education","healthcare","finance","law_enforcement"],"safety_requirements":[{"label":"pre_deployment_testing","confidence":0.95,"evidence":[{"quote":"Systems should undergo pre-deployment testing, risk identification and mitigation, and ongoing monitoring that demonstrate they are safe and effective based on their intended use","source_section":"Safe and Effective Systems"}]},{"label":"risk_assessment","confidence":0.95,"evidence":[{"quote":"Before deployment, and in a proactive and ongoing manner, potential risks of the automated system should be identified and mitigated.","source_section":"Safe and Effective Systems - What Should Be Expected"}]},{"label":"third_party_audit","confidence":0.9,"evidence":[{"quote":"Independent evaluation and reporting that confirms that the system is safe and effective, including reporting of steps taken to mitigate potential harms, should be performed and the results made public whenever possible.","source_section":"Safe and Effective Systems"}]},{"label":"transparency_disclosure","confidence":0.95,"evidence":[{"quote":"Designers, developers, and deployers of automated systems should provide generally accessible plain language documentation including clear descriptions of the overall system functioning and the role automation plays","source_section":"Notice and Explanation"}]},{"label":"human_oversight","confidence":0.95,"evidence":[{"quote":"You should be able to opt out from automated systems in favor of a human alternative, where appropriate... You should have access to timely human consideration and remedy by a fallback and escalation process","source_section":"Human Alternatives, Consideration, and Fallback"}]},{"label":"model_documentation","confidence":0.85,"evidence":[{"quote":"Entities responsible for the development or use of automated systems should provide regularly-updated reports that include: an overview of the system... a description of any data used to train machine learning models","source_section":"Safe and Effective Systems - Reporting"}]},{"label":"incident_reporting","confidence":0.8,"evidence":[{"quote":"ongoing monitoring procedures and regular performance testing reports, including monitoring frequency, results, and actions taken","source_section":"Safe and Effective Systems - Reporting"}]},{"label":"access_controls","confidence":0.75,"evidence":[{"quote":"Limit access to sensitive data and derived data. Sensitive data and derived data should not be sold, shared, or made public as part of data brokerage or other agreements.","source_section":"Data Privacy - Extra Protections for Sensitive Domains"}]}],"enforcement_mechanisms":[{"label":"none_specified","confidence":0.95,"evidence":[{"quote":"The Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights is non-binding and does not constitute U.S. government policy... does not require compliance with the principles described herein.","source_section":"Legal Disclaimer"}]},{"label":"soft_enforcement","confidence":0.8,"evidence":[{"quote":"The Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights is meant to assist governments and the private sector in moving principles into practice.","source_section":"Applying the Blueprint"}]}],"implementation_notes":"Document is explicitly non-binding per its legal disclaimer. It articulates five principles (safe and effective systems, algorithmic discrimination protections, data privacy, notice and explanation, human alternatives/fallback) with detailed technical guidance.
